fields.meta_title: Makeup Quiz: Find Your Everyday Look or Build One | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Take a free makeup quiz that names your everyday look in eight questions, then build one for a beauty brand, a bridal artist, or a class.
fields.h1: Build a Makeup Quiz for Beauty Brands and Makeup Artists
fields.hero_description: Build a makeup quiz that matches a look or a foundation shade, or take the eight-question one below to find your everyday look.
fields.features_heading: How a Makeup Quiz on Emergent Works
fields.features_subheading: A makeup quiz turns answers about routine, finish, and skin into one look or shade. Emergent builds the quiz and the table behind it.
fields.feature_1:
Match a look or score a test

Choose how answers count. In a look finder, every option points to one of your looks. In a class quiz, one option per question is correct, and the result is a total score.
fields.feature_2:
Shades listed on the result screen

Tag foundation, blush, and lip shades to each look in a product table. The result screen lists the shades tagged to that look, and a retagged shade shows up on the next result.
fields.feature_3:
One row for every finished quiz

The look, each option picked, and an email when someone offers one are saved as a row in a database you own. Filter for Bold Statement and read what those people chose.
fields.feature_4:
Sized for a thumb on a phone

Emergent builds the quiz as a conversational flow with one question per screen. Someone tapping in from a video link answers all eight without zooming in or scrolling sideways.
fields.feature_5:
An alert when a result needs an artist

Send an email or Slack alert when a result needs a person, such as a bride booking her makeup trial. The alert names her look and links to each answer she gave in the quiz.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and your code on paid plans

Host the quiz on your brand's own domain: custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository for a developer.

plan.angle: The top 10 is beauty brands' shade finders and routine quizzes plus BuzzFeed-style fun quizzes, with one quiz builder (Interact). A visitor can take an eight-question makeup quiz on this page that names their everyday look, then see four ways a beauty business runs one: a cosmetics brand matches a foundation shade from an undertone question, a bridal makeup artist reads each bride's result before the trial, a makeup teacher scores a ten-question class quiz and reteaches the most-missed question, and a makeup creator picks her next tutorial series from the result counts. The how-to covers results, undertone questions sourced to a cosmetics brand's guide, and testing; the FAQ covers free builds, question writing, answer keys for a class, and length.
tab_stories: Ines Hallam answers the shade finder on Verbena Row Cosmetics' site, says her wrist veins look green and she wants medium coverage, and her result screen shows foundation shade W32 with her email saved to the customer table.
Bridal makeup artist Petra Vance sends the quiz with every trial booking, and 7 days before Maren Quist's trial an email gives her Maren's Soft Glam result and her answer of no strip lashes.
Makeup teacher Joelle Marchetti gives her 18 students a ten-question quiz after the color theory lesson, sees that 11 of 18 missed question 6 on color correcting, and reteaches it the next Saturday.
Makeup creator Harriet Ennis links her quiz from every video, 2,600 viewers finish it in March with Soft Glam leading at 1,040, and she films a four-part Soft Glam series next.
